**3B.5 Research Note: Andrés Manuel López Obrador (2024)**

Bottom line: I found **some narrow, lawful uses of administrative control** around migration, but the stronger 2024 record points the other way: **surveillance, militarization, and detention practices were criticized as expansive, weakly accountable, and sometimes used to monitor critics or enable abuse**. I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence of a narrowly tailored, lawful emergency-powers regime; the direct evidence is sparse.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive, limited | Biden and AMLO agreed to coordinate immediate measures to reduce irregular border crossings while protecting human rights | Reuters | 2024-04-30 | https://theprint.in/world/us-mexico-to-clamp-down-on-illegal-immigration-leaders-say/2062785/ | Mexico and the U.S. agreed to concrete migration controls while explicitly pairing them with human-rights protection. This is the clearest evidence I found of a security-adjacent administrative control being framed narrowly rather than as blanket punishment. | 3B.5, 2B.1, 2B.7 |
| Positive, limited | Mexico signed an agreement with Venezuela to deport migrants and create work arrangements for them | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-03-21 | https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/mexico-reaches-agreement-with-venezuela-to-deport-migrants-3348403 | This was a formal bilateral administrative arrangement, not an ad hoc coercive measure. It shows one cross-border pressure point being handled through lawful negotiation and work arrangements. | 3B.5, 2B.7 |
| Negative | Mexico | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/mexico/freedom-net/2024 | Freedom House says the government used insecurity to justify expanding state surveillance with little accountability, and that a covert SEDENA cyberspace unit monitored critics using inauthentic accounts. This is direct negative evidence for surveillance used as control and intimidation. | 3B.5, 3B.2, 3B.3 |
| Negative | Mexico proposed constitutional changes threaten rights | Human Rights Watch | 2024-08-30 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/30/mexico-proposed-constitutional-changes-threaten-rights | HRW warned that the proposed changes could weaken judicial independence, expand military power, and erode privacy and transparency safeguards. That supports the view that coercive administrative tools were being widened rather than tightly constrained. | 3B.5, 2B.8, 3B.2, 3B.4 |
| Negative | Mexico | ONU-DH / UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention | 2024-09-17 | https://hchr.org.mx/relatorias_grupos/visita-a-mexico-informe-del-grupo-de-trabajo-sobre-la-detencion-arbitraria/ | The UN Working Group said arbitrary detention remained widespread, linked to ill-treatment, torture, disappearances, and arbitrary executions, and flagged military and navy detentions not entered in the registry. That is strong evidence that coercive control tools were not being used narrowly or lawfully. | 3B.5, 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.4 |
| Negative | Mexico’s military’s role in migrant massacre comes under sharp scrutiny | Reuters | 2024-10-16 | https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexico-militarys-role-in-migrant-massacre-comes-under-sharp-scrutiny-2024-10-16/ | Reuters reported soldiers killed six migrants and that the military’s account was disputed by local residents. This is direct evidence that security-force use could produce lethal abuse rather than narrow lawful control. | 3B.5, 3B.1, 2B.9, 3B.2 |
| Negative | Mexico: Flawed Inquiry on Soldiers’ Alleged Killing of Child | Human Rights Watch | 2024-08-28 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/28/mexico-flawed-inquiry-on-soldiers-alleged-killing-of-child | HRW said the Attorney General’s Office failed to properly investigate an alleged soldier-involved killing, ignored inconsistencies, and missed basic corroboration. That points to coercive systems without adequate lawful discipline or accountability. | 3B.5, 3B.4, 3B.1, 2B.9 |

**Assessment**

- **Best-supported positive reading:** some migration controls were handled through formal agreements and human-rights language.
- **Best-supported negative reading:** surveillance and detention practices in 2024 were criticized as broad, weakly accountable, and sometimes abusive.
- **Overall:** I would rate 3B.5 as **negative** for AMLO in 2024, with only narrow and indirect positive evidence.

**Search gap**

- I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence of a specific emergency decree, anti-terror measure, or security-law episode where AMLO clearly used those tools **narrowly and lawfully**.
- Most reliable 2024 material is instead about **surveillance expansion, militarization, and arbitrary detention**, so the record is uneven and weighted toward misuse concerns rather than lawful restraint.
